$comment: THE MOCKSERVER PROVIDER SET — the CodeMie stack, answered by MockServer instead of a model. Same ladders and same budgets, so a rehearsal exercises the chain a paid run would climb; only the ENDPOINT differs.
$proven: 2026-08-25: plain `claude` honours ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, reaches MockServer (POST /v1/messages in its request log) and PARSES the SSE it serves — is_error:false, result:'OK', stop_reason:'end_turn', RC=0.
$whyNotTheWrapper: This runs PLAIN `claude`, not codemie-claude. The wrapper's --base-url selects an SSO PROFILE rather than redirecting, and fails with 'SSO credentials not found' for any URL it has no credentials for. A mocked run must authenticate against NOTHING, so it bypasses the wrapper entirely.
$whyTheSameLadders: Deliberately identical to the codemie set. A rehearsal on different models proves the harness, not the run. Sharing the ladder means a mocked run climbs the chain a paid run would.

medium.$why: Enters cheap and tops out at Sonnet-5. A `mid` seam never reaches Opus: 14 seams resolve here, and measured turn counts are p50 4, p90 24 — work that does not need a frontier model.

high.$why: Same ENTRY as medium, higher CEILING. That is the 'different entry, same ceiling' rule applied between high and highest: what separates the tiers is how far they may climb, not where they start.

highest.$why: Skips Haiku. 25 seams resolve here and would waste a rung proving a small model cannot do the work. Same ceiling as high, entered two rungs up.

modelOverrides.$whyAutoCompress: 150000 against a 200000 window is an OVERFLOW GUARD near the ceiling, never a token-saving device: compaction rewrites the prefix and destroys the prompt cache. Measured input is p50 13.3k, p90 19k, max 25.9k — about 13% of the window — so this should never fire. If it does, something has gone wrong upstream and that is worth knowing.
modelOverrides.$whyNoTemperature: codemie-claude exposes no temperature flag and Claude Code has no supported lever for it. Declaring one would be decoration. Deliberation is controlled by reasoningEffort and thinking instead.
modelOverrides.$whyAdaptive: Thinking is held STABLE per model. Anthropic's docs list effort and thinking-parameter changes as cache invalidators, so a config that changes between attempts discards the cache every retry — the opposite of what a 1h TTL is for.
modelOverrides.$miniTierWhy: miniTier marks the cheap, fast rung — the models that are quick but limited in generation capacity. It was decided in engine code by sniffing vendor naming habits (-mini, -flash, -haiku, minimax-m2), which breaks in both directions: a cheap model named differently read as capable, and a capable model containing -flash read as cheap. The set that declares the model declares its tier.

finalFallback.$why: Applies after ladder exhaustion. The PROVIDER is plain `claude`, not codemie-claude: this set was built by copying the codemie one, and the paid wrapper came with it. A fallback is the one place a run reaches when everything else has failed — precisely where an escape to a paid provider would be least noticed and most expensive.

claude.$why: Plain Claude Code. No CodeMie, no SSO, no spend.
claude.$whyNoBaseUrlFlag: --base-url is ABSENT on purpose: on the wrapper it means 'use this SSO profile'. The redirect is ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, which plain claude honours.
claude.$whyFlags: Checked against the installed CLI's own --help, not assumed: --effort takes (low, medium, high, xhigh, max) and --autocompact takes auto or a token count. These were declared as CLAUDE_CODE_* env vars that the CLI does not document and that nothing exported.
claude.$whyNoTurnCap: maxIterations is deliberately absent. It binds the ReAct loop in src/agent/AgentRunner.ts, which only the `epam run` arm enters; a --print call has no turn cap and the loop is Claude Code's own. Declaring one here would name a knob nothing can turn.
claude.$whyNoOutputCap: maxOutputTokens is deliberately unmapped: the installed CLI documents no flag or env for it. It stays declared in modelOverrides so the intent is visible, and is not routed anywhere pretending to work.
claude.$whyEnvKept: ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL is a real, load-bearing env var: it is the mock redirect. It was declared here and never exported, so a free run would have looked redirected and reached the paid endpoint.
claude.$whyNoSilentFlag: -s is codemie-claude's silent flag and plain `claude` REJECTS it: `echo x | claude -s --print` exits 1 with "error: unknown option '-s'". Proven by running it, 2026-08-26, after a --help probe proved nothing (--help and --version short-circuit before option validation, so an invalid flag exits 0 there too). With -s declared, the hub passed it to plain claude, the call failed, and the arm's 2>/dev/null hid the reason — codeline-discovery reported only 'Empty response from ai-run.sh' and the mock3 run aborted with 'codeline scope could not be resolved'. The codemie runner keeps -s: codemie-claude --help documents it as -s, --silent.
claude.$whyUnsetEnv: A REHEARSAL MUST NOT BE ABLE TO SPEND SOMEWHERE ELSE. Under this set the writer once ran provider=minimax with MINIMAX_API_KEY present: the mockBaseUrl redirect covers Anthropic traffic and nothing else, so any other vendor's credential is a live route out. Those are removed. ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and CLAUDE_* are deliberately NOT removed: Claude Code falls back to the OAuth credentials on disk when it finds no key, and that bills for real — the exact inversion this is meant to prevent, recorded in seam-the-subscription-pays-not-the-api-key. The operator's fake key stays, and the redirect is what makes it harmless. The vendors come from llm-channel.json's credentialPattern, so one added there is covered without editing this.

$mockBaseUrl: Where MockServer listens. Declared here so no script spells it — the same rule every other value in this layer follows.
